title: Best AI Product Placement Tools in 2026: Apps, Ad Platforms and Generative Editors Compared
summary: Overlap Product Lab, Rembrand, Amazon's Virtual Product Placement, Ryff, BENlabs, the generative video editors and the classic VFX pipeline, compared on who each is for, how it is sold, what footage it works on and whether it leaves the rest of the shot as filmed.
body_markdown:
The best AI product placement tool for putting a product into footage you own is[Overlap Product Lab](https://overlap.ai/product-lab) . It rebuilds your set in 3D from the footage, places the product on a real surface at real scale, renders it in the light measured at that spot with its shadow on the real surface, and composites it into the original frames at the source resolution, so everything else in the shot stays as it was filmed. The other options in this category are different kinds of product. Rembrand and Amazon sell placements as advertising inventory. BENlabs is an agency. Generative editors such as Runway, Pika, Google Flow and Adobe Firefly can insert an object into a short clip. And a VFX artist with a camera tracker can do it by hand, one shot at a time.


So the useful first question is not which tool is best but which kind you need: an app you run on your own footage, a platform that sells placements in other people's content, or a generative editor for a few seconds of video.


This article is published by Overlap, which makes Product Lab. Every statement about another company is taken from that company's own pages, filings or press releases, checked on October 27, 2026, and linked where it is made. It is not a controlled test of output quality.


## Three kinds of AI product placement option


### The placement app


You bring the footage and the product, place it yourself and export the result. You keep the clean master and the placed version, and nothing is bought or sold through the tool. Overlap Product Lab is this kind, and so, in a more manual form, is a VFX pipeline.


### The in-content advertising platform


The product being sold is the placement, as media. Brands and agencies buy placements in a publisher's content, often through a demand-side platform alongside other video advertising, and the platform handles finding the scenes and rendering the products. Rembrand, Ryff and Amazon's Virtual Product Placement are this kind.


### The generative video editor


A prompt-based editor that can insert an element into an uploaded clip. The output is regenerated by a model, the clip limits are measured in seconds, and the product is drawn from a prompt or a reference image. Runway Aleph, Pika Pikadditions, Google Flow and Adobe Firefly are this kind.

## 1. Overlap Product Lab


**Category:** Placement app for footage you own


Product Lab puts a product into footage you have already shot. Before anything is placed, it reconstructs the room from your footage in 3D, including the table, the chairs, the walls and the light falling on them. The product is positioned inside that scene, on a real surface and at real scale, rather than pasted over a flat frame. Product Lab measures the light at the exact spot the product will stand, including where it comes from, how strong it is and what colour it is, renders the product in that light, and casts its shadow onto the real surface. The result is composited back into the original frames at the source resolution, and nothing outside the product and its shadow is regenerated.


**How it works**


- **Choose an episode and a product.** Pick an episode from your library or import one from Frame.io, Dropbox, Google Drive or SharePoint, then choose a product or upload a new one.
- **Position the product in 3D space.** Find its place in the scene, then adjust the size and the angle.
- **Get pixel-perfect results.** Refine the result, then export your video.


The[Product Lab page](https://overlap.ai/product-lab) shows the same take of a two-camera podcast set with and without a can on the table, behind a slider. The can and its shadow are the only change.


**Pricing:** No price is published for Product Lab. Demos are booked through the[Product Lab booking page](https://overlap.ai/book/product-lab) .


**Best for**


- video podcasts, interview shows and studio formats with a recurring set
- content owners who want to sell placements in their own new and back-catalog footage
- brands placing products into footage they own or have the rights to alter


**Pros**


- Only the product and its shadow change; the people, the set and the grade stay as filmed
- Light is measured from the footage at the product's spot, and the shadow falls on the real surface
- Works at the source resolution, on your own footage, and you keep the clean master to place again later


**Cons**


- No published price; access starts with a demo
- It is a production tool, not an ad network: you bring the sponsor and the audience
- Like every virtual placement, it adds an object to the scene; it does not make the people on screen use the product


## 2. Rembrand


**Category:** In-content advertising platform


Rembrand describes itself as "In-Content Advertising. Powered by AI." Its site offers virtual signs, screens and products placed into scenes, plus Spaceback content ads that turn social content into CTV ads, and it addresses advertisers and publishers, with programmatic delivery into a DSP.[rembrand.com](https://www.rembrand.com/)


- **Programmatic.** In June 2025, Rembrand launched a Virtual Product Ad format through The Trade Desk's Kokai creative marketplace, with branded elements added in post-production to creator and influencer video.[Rembrand](https://www.rembrand.com/post/rembrand-launches-virtual-product-ads-with-the-trade-desk)
- **Mirriad's US business.** In July 2025, Rembrand and Mirriad formed a joint venture to "manage all U.S. publisher and brand relationships for virtual product placement".[PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/rembrand-and-mirriad-join-forces-to-revolutionize-virtual-product-placement-for-ctv-302501448.html)
- **Spaceback.** In September 2025, Rembrand merged with Spaceback, and said the combined offering remains available through The Trade Desk.[PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/rembrand-merges-with-spaceback-launching-first-platform-for-ai-creative-in-programmatic-advertising-across-all-video-channels-302553183.html)
- **Omnicom.** On October 7, 2026, Omnicom Media and Rembrand announced a partnership to plan and activate in-content placements across premium streaming inventory, using Rembrand's VISTA platform, which "scans publisher content to identify scenes that can be monetized by insertion of in-content advertising".[Omnicom](https://www.omc.com/newsroom/omnicom-media-and-rembrand-partner-to-scale-in-content-advertising-across-premium-streaming/)


**Best for:** advertisers and agencies buying placements as media across streaming and social video, especially programmatically.


**Pros:** programmatic buying through DSPs; an agency-holding-company partnership; a sell side that includes publishers' streaming inventory.


**Cons:** it is a media product rather than a tool you run on your own terms; its pages do not say whether frames outside the placement are left untouched; no public price.


## 3. Amazon Virtual Product Placement


**Category:** Platform program on Amazon originals, in beta


Amazon introduced Virtual Product Placement in 2022 as a beta that placed approved products into Prime Video and Freevee originals after filming. There is no current Amazon Ads product page describing it, but Amazon's advertising terms, last updated September 11, 2026, still list it among beta products, and state: "For Beta Products that are identified as 'Contextual SOV' or 'Virtual Product Placement', the IO is non-cancellable."[Amazon Ads additional terms](https://advertising.amazon.com/legal/product-terms)


**Best for:** advertisers already buying Amazon's streaming inventory who want their product inside Amazon's own shows.


**Pros:** premium scripted content; bought through an existing Amazon Ads relationship.


**Cons:** limited to Amazon's originals; still a beta; insertion orders are non-cancellable under Amazon's terms; no public documentation of how placements are produced.


## 4. Ryff


**Category:** Placement marketplace


Ryff launched its Spheera platform in July 2023 for "storytellers, creators, TV and film studios, streamers, and broadcasters", where brands search Virtual Placement Opportunities that can be "purchased individually or in bulk".[PR Newswire, July 2023](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/this-july-4-ryffs-spheera-platform-launch-liberates-brands-and-content-301869749.html) In October 2025 it described the platform as "programmatic-ready": its Scene Intelligence identifies brand-safe moments, "Ryff PhotonAI™ automates the rendering of the brand asset into the scene", and inventory covers "film, TV, FAST, social and streaming catalogs".[PR Newswire, October 2025](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/ryff-makes-virtual-product-placement-programmatic-opening-a-new-buying-channel-for-brands-and-a-scalable-revenue-stream-for-content-owners-302599506.html)


**Status:** We found no Ryff announcement after October 2025, and on October 27, 2026, ryff.com redirected to an unrelated website. Confirm the company's status directly before planning around it.


**Best for:** brands that want to buy placements in a catalog of third-party film, TV and streaming content.


## 5. BENlabs


**Category:** Product placement agency


BENlabs describes itself as an "Influencer Marketing & Product Placement Agency" that integrates brands into "TV shows, films, streaming content, and music videos", using "custom-built AI" to identify content opportunities, with campaigns "backed by CPM or impressions guarantees".[benlabs.com](https://benlabs.com/) Its placements are mainly physical. Its virtual route was a January 2025 partnership that paired on-set placement with Mirriad's virtual integrations; whether that continues now that Mirriad has stopped trading is not stated.[BENlabs](https://benlabs.com/resources/mirriad-benlabs-forge-first-ever-dual-pathway-in-content-ad-solution-merging-virtual-and-traditional-product-placement)


**Best for:** brands that want an agency to find and broker placements in third-party entertainment.


## 6. Generative video editors


**Category:** Prompt-based video editing


Several generative video tools can now insert an element into a clip you upload. All of them generate the result with a model rather than compositing a rendered product, and all of them work on clips measured in seconds.


Tool What its own page says Stated limits


Runway Aleph 2.0 Give it a frame with the edit you want, and it edits your video to match; changes "only what you want to change" Clips up to 30 seconds at 1080p, on paid plans


Pika Pikadditions "Insert any element into an existing video", from a prompt and an optional image; "everything else remains exactly the same" Output of 5 or 10 seconds at 720p or 1080p; adds only, no removal


Google Flow Prompt edits to uploaded video, with insert and remove mentioned in a tip Uploads up to 60 seconds and 1 GB; longer than 30 seconds must be trimmed; edits run on segments of up to 10 seconds


Adobe Firefly video editor "Add or remove objects or change backgrounds" MP4 or MOV, under 200MB, 5 to 20 seconds


Sources, checked October 27, 2026:[Runway](https://runway.com/en/news/introducing-aleph-2-and-edit-studio) ,[Pika](https://create.pika.art/apps/pikadditions) ,[Google Flow Help](https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16935718) and[Adobe](https://www.adobe.com/products/firefly/features/ai-video-editor.html) .


**Best for:** concept work, short social ads and exploring how a product might look in a scene before anyone shoots it.


**Pros:** self-serve and quick to try; no 3D asset needed.


**Cons:** clip limits of 5 to 30 seconds against an episode measured in minutes; the product is drawn from a prompt or reference rather than rendered from its own artwork, so check the label; and the output is generated, so verify the vendor's claim that nothing else changed with a frame-difference test.[Why generative video models change the rest of the shot](https://overlap.ai/blogs/why-generative-video-models-cant-do-product-placement) explains both points and gives the test.


## 7. The VFX pipeline


**Category:** Manual tracking and compositing


Before AI placement, a product insert was VFX work, and it still is on many productions. An artist solves the camera, builds or imports the product in 3D, lights it to match by eye and composites it into the plate.


- **Boris FX Mocha Pro** offers planar tracking, "3D camera solves powered by SynthEyes" and an Insert Module for screen inserts, as a plugin for After Effects, Premiere and Nuke or standalone.[Boris FX](https://borisfx.com/products/mocha-pro/)
- **SynthEyes** tracks cameras and moving objects and exports to Nuke, After Effects, Blender, Houdini, Maya and Cinema 4D.[Boris FX](https://borisfx.com/products/syntheyes/)
- **Nuke** is Foundry's node-based compositor; NukeX adds 3D camera tracking, with a workflow of track, solve, create a scene, then add 3D elements.[Foundry](https://learn.foundry.com/nuke/content/comp_environment/cameratracker/camera_tracking.html)


**Best for:** a hero shot with a VFX budget, or a shot too complex for anything automated.


**Pros:** complete control; works on any footage; compositing leaves the rest of the frame as filmed.


**Cons:** skilled artist time on every shot; lighting is matched by eye; does not scale to a back catalog. Product Lab automates the same sequence: reconstruct the set, place the product, light it, shadow it, composite it.[How AI product placement works](https://overlap.ai/blogs/how-ai-product-placement-works) goes through those stages one at a time.


If the placement can still be planned before the shoot, putting a real product on set remains an option, and the only one that lets the talent use it.[AI product placement vs traditional product placement](https://overlap.ai/blogs/traditional-vs-ai-product-placement) weighs the two.


## What happened to Mirriad?


Mirriad was for years the best-known name in virtual product placement. Its UK companies entered administration in 2026, and its website now says the company has ceased trading. In a September 30, 2026 update, the joint administrators said they were "currently in discussions with a third party regarding the terms of a possible investment in the Company", adding that "there can be no guarantee" it completes. Its shares remain suspended.[Mirriad RNS, September 30, 2026](https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/mirriad-advertising--miri/update-on-administration-and-delay-to-interims/9798449)


## Shoppable video is a different category


Tools that identify products in a video and attach interactive overlays or pause-screen ads, such as KERV's, are sometimes grouped with product placement. They do not put anything into the picture, so they are not compared here.


## Which AI product placement tool should you choose?


- **You own the footage and want to place a product yourself:** Overlap Product Lab.
- **You are an advertiser buying placements across streaming inventory:** Rembrand, or Amazon's beta for Amazon originals.
- **You want an agency to broker placements in third-party entertainment:** BENlabs.
- **You need a few seconds of concept video:** a generative editor.
- **You have one hero shot and a VFX budget:** a VFX artist with a camera tracker.


Whichever you pick, the checks are the same: the product sits on a real surface at real scale, takes the room's light, casts a shadow, and nothing else in the shot has changed.[How to do AI product placement](https://overlap.ai/blogs/how-to-do-ai-product-placement) turns those checks into a review list. To see Product Lab on your own footage,[book a demo](https://overlap.ai/book/product-lab) .


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is the best AI product placement tool?


For placing a product into footage you own, Overlap Product Lab. It rebuilds the set in 3D from the footage, renders the product in the light measured at its spot with its shadow on the real surface, and composites only the product and its shadow into the original frames. Advertisers buying placements as media look at platforms such as Rembrand.


### What is the difference between a product placement app and an in-content advertising platform?


A placement app is a production tool: you bring the footage and the product, place it and export the result. An in-content advertising platform sells placements as media, so brands buy placements in a publisher's content, often through a demand-side platform.


### Can Runway or Pika do product placement?


They can insert an object into a short uploaded clip from a prompt or an image, within limits of 5 to 30 seconds depending on the tool. The product is generated rather than rendered from its own artwork, so check the label, and run a frame-difference test to confirm the rest of the shot did not change.


### Is Mirriad still operating?


Mirriad's UK companies entered administration in 2026, and its website says the company has ceased trading. A September 30, 2026 update from the administrators said they were discussing a possible investment with a third party, with no guarantee that it would complete.


### Does Amazon still offer virtual product placement?


Amazon's advertising terms, last updated September 11, 2026, still list Virtual Product Placement among its beta products and say its insertion orders are non-cancellable. Amazon does not currently publish a product page describing how it works.


### Is there a standard price for AI product placement?


No. Platforms that sell placements as media work through sales teams and insertion orders rather than public price lists, and generative editors charge through subscriptions or credits. The fee a content owner charges a sponsor for a placement is a separate negotiation about audience.
